derive:0.en: Inside the Herb Pavilion, Master Qingwu pointed to a pale root soaking in still water. 'Every healing power we use,' she said softly, 'we *derive* from the living plant itself, not from our own will.' I cupped the jar and felt a faint warmth rise through the glass.
derive:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，所有疗愈之力都____自草药本身，而非弟子的意志。
derive:0.hook: The root pulsed once, then went perfectly still.
derive:0.line: 'We *derive* nothing from pride, only from patience.'

report:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a long scroll across the low table. It was his season-end *report* on the Herb Pavilion's rarest seedlings — columns of brushwork listing each plant's growth, fragrance, and spiritual warmth. He tapped one entry and looked at me without a word.
report:0.cnHint: 师兄将一份关于灵植园珍稀幼苗的____摊开在桌上，其中一条记录让他沉默不语。
report:0.hook: The entry he pointed to bore my name.
report:0.line: 'Your *report* is missing the night-bloom observation, junior.'

research:0.en: Xiaoxing sat cross-legged among rows of clay pots, ink still wet on her fingers. Her *research* on how moonlight affected root depth had filled three scrolls already. She hummed a quiet note, and two seedlings seemed to lean toward her voice.
research:0.cnHint: 师妹正在进行一项关于月光如何影响草药根系的____，已经写满了三卷竹简。
research:0.hook: Outside, the moon slipped behind a cloud that had not been there before.
research:0.line: 'My *research* shows that silence grows stronger roots.'

different:0.en: Master Qingwu placed two identical jars side by side. The herbs inside looked the same, yet their scent was *different* — one smelled of rain, the other of stone. 'Your senses will teach you what your eyes cannot,' she said, and left me alone with the choice.
different:0.cnHint: 两株看起来一模一样的草药，气味却____，师尊让我独自分辨。
different:0.hook: I reached for one jar, and the other trembled.
different:0.line: 'A *different* scent means a different fate — choose carefully.'

author:0.en: On the highest shelf of the Herb Pavilion rested a crumbling text. Shen Wujiu told me the *author* was a disciple who had vanished three generations ago, leaving behind only formulas no one had yet dared use. Dust rose when I touched the cover.
author:0.cnHint: 灵植园最高架上有一部古籍，其____三代前已失踪，留下了无人敢用的秘方。
author:0.hook: One formula was underlined in fresh ink.
author:0.line: 'The *author* left no name, only a warning at the end.'

increase:0.en: Xiaoxing measured the luminous moss every morning. Over seven days she had watched its glow *increase* from a faint shimmer to a light strong enough to read by. She smiled, but Master Qingwu's brow stayed creased as she studied the numbers.
increase:0.cnHint: 师妹记录到苔藓的光芒____得异乎寻常，而师尊的眉头却越皱越紧。
increase:0.hook: By evening the glow was brighter than any lamp in the pavilion.
increase:0.line: 'An *increase* this fast is never a gift — it is a question.'

university:0.en: A sealed letter arrived at the Herb Pavilion bearing the crest of the Grand Cloud Academy, the great *university* of the upper peaks where masters sent only their finest disciples. Master Qingwu set it on the table without opening it and looked at each of us in turn.
university:0.cnHint: 一封来自上峰大学府的密信送到了灵植园，师尊将信放在桌上，依次看了我们每一个人。
university:0.hook: Only one of us would be called to answer it.
university:0.line: 'The *university* above the clouds accepts one name per generation.'

turn:0.en: I was grinding dried petals when the air in the Herb Pavilion began to *turn* cold without reason. The flame under the copper pot shrank, the leaves on their stems curled inward, and somewhere behind the shelves a single jar rolled and stopped. I did not move.
turn:0.cnHint: 我研磨花瓣时，灵植园的空气忽然____凉，架后有一只瓶无故滚动后停下。
turn:0.hook: A voice I did not recognize said my name.
turn:0.line: 'Do not *turn* around until the cold has passed — not yet.'

less:0.en: The spirit herb garden stretched across the inner hall, rows of glowing plants breathing soft light. Master Qingwu walked the rows slowly, pinching leaves and frowning. 'Most disciples use far too many words,' she said. 'The rarest formulas need *less*, not more — one pure syllable can do what a hundred cluttered ones cannot.' I counted my own words and said nothing.
less:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，最强的法诀需要____的字，而非更多。
less:0.hook: One cold herb at the row's end had no glow at all.

information:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me through the seedling shelves, naming each plant in a low voice. Every leaf carried *information* about the season it had grown in — a jagged edge meant drought, a silver vein meant a year of high wind. I pressed my finger to one silver vein and felt a distant mountain storm pass through my palm.
information:0.cnHint: 师兄说每片叶子都携带着关于它生长季节的____。
information:0.hook: One leaf had a vein I could not name, shaped like a closed eye.
information:0.line: 'Every vein carries *information* the formula needs to work.'

paragraph:0.en: Master Qingwu handed me a slip of bark. On it, a single *paragraph* of cultivation text shimmered in green ink — twelve words that described how to ask a herb for its healing power rather than simply take it. I read the lines three times. On the third reading, the nearest plant turned slowly toward me, as if it had heard.
paragraph:0.cnHint: 师尊给了我一张树皮，上面写着一____修炼文字，教我如何向灵草借力。
paragraph:0.hook: The green ink had not yet dried, though the bark was decades old.
paragraph:0.line: 'Read this *paragraph* once more before you touch any root.'

look:0.en: Xiaoxing crouched beside a pale fern, her lantern held low. 'You have to *look* the way water looks at stone,' she said, 'not hunting, just resting your eyes until the plant shows you its name.' I stilled my breath and tried. For one moment the fern's outline blurred, then sharpened into a character I had never been taught.
look:0.cnHint: 师妹教我用一种特别的方式____灵草，直到它自己显出名字。
look:0.hook: The character the fern showed me matched nothing in my textbook.
look:0.line: '*Look* the way rain looks — patient, with no intention.'

benefit:0.en: I asked Shen Wujiu why we tended the herbs by hand instead of using a word-formula to water them all at once. He smiled and set down his pail. 'The *benefit* of slow tending is that the plant learns your breathing,' he said. 'A herb that knows your breath will answer you faster in the field.' His own herbs leaned faintly toward him as he spoke.
benefit:0.cnHint: 师兄解释说，亲手照料灵草的____是它会记住你的呼吸。
benefit:0.hook: The herb nearest his hand bloomed two weeks ahead of its season.
benefit:0.line: 'The real *benefit* is the herb remembering who you are.'

contain:0.en: Master Qingwu lifted a sealed clay jar from the shelf and set it before me. 'This jar must *contain* three living syllables at once without letting them merge,' she said. 'If they merge, the formula becomes something none of us can predict.' I placed my hands on the cool clay and felt three tiny pulses pushing outward, each one testing the walls.
contain:0.cnHint: 师尊让我用一只陶罐____三个活音节，不能让它们合并。
contain:0.hook: One pulse was already moving faster than the other two.
contain:0.line: 'You must *contain* those syllables as long as it takes.'

direction:0.en: The seed rows ran east to west, but Xiaoxing showed me that each plant faced a slightly different *direction* depending on which wind carried its original spore. 'Match your formula to that angle,' she said, 'or the words arrive as a stranger.' I knelt and tilted my mouth to follow the fern's lean, and this time the healing warmth came without effort.
direction:0.cnHint: 师妹说每株植物面朝不同的____，施法时必须与它的朝向对齐。
direction:0.hook: At the room's far end, one seedling faced directly inward — toward us.
direction:0.line: 'Speak in the same *direction* the plant already faces.'

attach:0.en: Shen Wujiu showed me how to *attach* a written word-tag to a herb's stem without breaking its spirit flow — fold the paper along the grain, press gently, never pierce. The tag would hold the plant's formula-name so even a new disciple could read it at a glance. I attached mine carefully. The stem accepted it, and a faint hum rose up through my fingertips.
attach:0.cnHint: 师兄教我如何把写有名字的纸签____到灵草茎上，而不打断它的灵气流动。
attach:0.hook: The last stem in the row had a tag already — in handwriting I did not recognise.
attach:0.line: '*Attach* the tag gently — the stem is still listening.'

end:0.en: The herb rows stretched the full length of the spirit garden, each plant glowing faintly in the morning mist. I walked slowly, reading their names aloud as Master Qingwu had taught me. At the far *end* of the last row stood a single black stalk I had never seen before, its leaves curled tight as a closed fist.
end:0.cnHint: 灵植园的最深处，我发现了一株从未见过的黑色草药，叶片紧紧卷曲。
end:0.hook: The black stalk had no name written beside it.
end:0.line: 'Walk to the *end* of the row before you touch anything,' said Master Qingwu.

important:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me a small clay pot and whispered that what grew inside was the most *important* herb in the whole garden. Its white petals held a single drop of light, like a captured star. I cupped it with both hands, afraid even my breath might disturb it.
important:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我，这株草药对灵植园来说至关重要，我小心翼翼地捧住它。
important:0.hook: The drop of light inside the petal suddenly trembled.
important:0.line: 'This one is *important* — do not let it touch the soil,' Xiaoxing said softly.

cause:0.en: Shen Wujiu warned me that speaking a word-formula too loudly near the young herbs could *cause* their roots to burn. I lowered my voice to a murmur. The nearest seedling still shivered, its green light flickering like a candle in wind.
cause:0.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，在幼苗旁大声念咒语会伤害它们的根系，我赶紧压低了声音。
cause:0.hook: A thin line of smoke rose from the seedling's stem.
cause:0.line: 'Too much force will *cause* the roots to split,' Shen Wujiu said quietly.

accord:0.en: Master Qingwu asked each of us to tend one row in *accord* with the herb's own nature — water plants near water, fire plants near warmth. I chose the row of frost ferns and breathed slowly, keeping my spirit calm and cool. They opened their fronds one by one.
accord:0.cnHint: 师尊让我们按照每株草药的本性来照料，我选择了霜蕨，努力与它的天性保持一致。
accord:0.hook: The last frost fern refused to open, no matter how still I stood.
accord:0.line: 'Work in *accord* with the herb, not against it,' Master Qingwu said.

result:0.en: I had watered the spirit moss three times that morning, following every step in the old text. The *result* was a soft golden glow spreading outward from the moss bed, filling the whole room with warmth. Xiaoxing clapped once, eyes wide with surprise and delight.
result:0.cnHint: 我按照古籍认真照料灵苔，结果它散发出金色光芒，充满了整个房间。
result:0.hook: But the glow faded at the window, as if something outside refused the warmth.
result:0.line: 'Is this the *result* you expected?' Xiaoxing asked, pointing at the glowing moss.

recent:0.en: Shen Wujiu pointed to a row of pale herbs whose leaves had begun to curl at the edges. He said their *recent* growth had slowed without clear reason, and Master Qingwu had been watching them in silence for three days. Something in the soil had changed.
recent:0.cnHint: 师兄指着一排叶缘卷曲的草药，说它们最近的生长明显迟缓，原因不明。
recent:0.hook: Master Qingwu's footsteps stopped beside that very row at dusk.
recent:0.line: 'Their *recent* colour troubles me,' Shen Wujiu said, frowning at the pale leaves.

start:0.en: Master Qingwu told us that every great formula had a humble *start*: a single seed word planted in still air. She pressed one seed into my palm and said nothing more. I stood in the center of the garden, closed my eyes, and spoke the word for the first time.
start:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每个伟大的咒语都有一个朴素的开始——我握着那颗种子字，鼓起勇气开口了。
start:0.hook: The ground under my feet hummed, as though the garden had been waiting.
start:0.line: 'Every path has a *start* — speak the seed word and listen,' said Master Qingwu.

however:0.en: The spirit herbs needed silence to absorb morning light, and I had kept perfectly still for an hour. *However*, when the temple bell rang across the clouds, every plant in the garden turned sharply toward the sound, leaves trembling, as if the bell carried a warning only they could hear.
however:0.cnHint: 我在灵植园里静静守候了一个时辰，然而寺钟一响，所有草药竟同时转向钟声，叶片颤抖。
however:0.hook: The bell rang again, but this time no echo came back from the clouds.
however:0.line: 'I thought them calm — *however*, they sense something we do not,' Xiaoxing said.

human:0.en: The Spirit Herb Garden smelled of rain and old ink. Rows of glowing plants lined the stone shelves, each one a living word waiting to be learned. Master Qingwu knelt beside a pale silver fern. 'Every *human* hand that tends these herbs,' she said softly, 'leaves a little of its warmth behind.' The fern's leaves curled gently toward her fingers. Above the garden's single window, a cloud shaped like an open palm drifted past and did not move on.
human:0.cnHint: 师尊说，每一双____的手照料这些灵草，都会留下温度。
human:0.hook: The cloud outside held its shape far too long.
human:0.line: 'A *human* touch is the first lesson these herbs will teach you.'

large:0.en: The inner hall of the Spirit Herb Garden held a single *large* basin carved from pale mountain stone. Shen Wujiu told me it could hold enough morning dew to fill the whole sect's supply for a season. Today it stood dry and cracked. Xiaoxing pressed her palm to its rim and frowned. 'Something drew all the water out overnight,' she whispered. A faint hum rose from the basin's empty center, low and steady, like a held breath.
large:0.cnHint: 灵植园内有一个____的石盆，昨夜水全部消失了。
large:0.hook: The hum grew louder the moment we stepped back.
large:0.line: 'A basin this *large* should never run dry in a single night.'

actually:0.en: The herb garden smelled of rain and old pine. Rows of silver-leafed plants lined the stone shelves, each one a living word waiting to be learned. I had expected simple weeding work, but Master Qingwu told me the task was *actually* a test — every plant I touched would reveal whether my spiritual sense was true or hollow.
actually:0.cnHint: 我以为只是普通的除草活，师尊却说这____是一场考验。
actually:0.hook: One silver leaf had already turned black at my touch.
actually:0.line: 'This is *actually* your first lesson, not a chore.'

themselves:0.en: Along the inner wall of the herb garden, rare spirit-mosses grew in sealed glass jars. Shen Wujiu explained that these mosses could heal *themselves* when cracked, drawing words of mending from the air around them. I pressed my finger to one jar and felt the soft pulse of living syllables pushing back.
themselves:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，那些灵苔能够____自我愈合，从空气中汲取愈合之词。
themselves:0.hook: A hairline crack appeared in the glass where no crack had been before.
themselves:0.line: 'These mosses *themselves* know the word for healing.'

person:0.en: Master Qingwu moved between the rows without bending a single stem. She said only one *person* in a generation could hear the low hum of a dying herb before it wilted, and that such a gift was both a blessing and a burden. The garden fell quiet, and I realized every plant had turned its leaves toward me.
person:0.cnHint: 师尊说，每一代中只有一个____能听见灵草垂死前的低鸣。
person:0.hook: Every leaf in the garden was pointed at me now.
person:0.line: 'Only one *person* per generation hears that sound.'

without:0.en: Xiaoxing moved through the garden *without* a sound, her fingers barely grazing the herb tips as she named each one in a soft breath. She had memorized all three hundred plants before the first snow of her arrival year. I watched her and felt the gap between us like a cold wind off the cloud sea below.
without:0.cnHint: 师妹____发出任何声音地穿行于园中，轻声为每株灵草命名。
without:0.hook: She paused at the last row and did not name one plant.
without:0.line: 'You must move *without* hesitation or the herb will close.'

among:0.en: I was set to sort a basket of dried herbs by their spiritual tone. *Among* the pale bundles lay one sprig of deep violet — a word-herb I had never seen in any lesson scroll. Shen Wujiu watched from the doorway without speaking. The violet sprig was warm to the touch, as if it held a small fire inside.
among:0.cnHint: 在一篮干燥灵草____，我发现了一株从未在课卷中见过的深紫色草药。
among:0.hook: Shen Wujiu's expression shifted when I reached for the violet sprig.
among:0.line: '*Among* all the herbs here, that one was not placed by me.'

suppose:0.en: The lesson asked me to water the spirit-root seedlings in order of their spoken names. I did not know the order, so I had to *suppose* which name came first by the color of each seedling's glow. Three glowed gold; one glowed a pale and trembling white. I chose wrong, and the white seedling let out a single sharp sound like a struck bell.
suppose:0.cnHint: 我不知道顺序，只能____哪株灵根苗的名字排在最前，结果选错了。
suppose:0.hook: That bell-sound echoed far longer than it should have.
suppose:0.line: 'I *suppose* the white one speaks before the gold.'

health:0.en: Master Qingwu held a withered herb up to the light filtering through the garden's paper window. She said a plant's *health* was a record of every word spoken near it — harsh words left brown edges, calm words kept the stem straight. I thought of every careless thing I had ever said and felt a quiet shame settle over me.
health:0.cnHint: 师尊说，灵草的____记录着它身旁所说的每一个字，言语轻率则叶缘枯黄。
health:0.hook: The herb in her hand had very few straight stems left.
health:0.line: 'Its *health* tells me what words were used in this room.'

mean:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a scroll and asked what the symbol at its center was meant to *mean*. I said it looked like the word for wind, but he shook his head. In the herb garden, that same symbol appeared burned into the soil between two rows, faint and fresh. No one had been there since morning.
mean:0.cnHint: 师兄问我卷轴中心的符文____什么，我猜错了，而那个符文随后出现在了泥土里。
mean:0.hook: The burned symbol in the soil was still warm.
mean:0.line: 'What do you think this symbol is meant to *mean*?'

likely:0.en: The spirit-herb garden stretched across the inner hall, each plant glowing with a faint green pulse. Master Qingwu moved between the rows, studying each leaf. She paused before a silver-veined fern and beckoned me closer. 'A disciple who tends this herb with care is *likely* to form their first word-formula within the month,' she said softly. The fern's glow deepened as if it had heard her.
likely:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊在灵植园中暗示，用心照料这株草药的弟子____在一个月内凝成第一道字诀。
likely:0.hook: That night, the fern's silver veins began to spell a shape.
likely:0.line: 'A disciple who tends this herb with care is *likely* to form their first word-formula within the month.'

experience:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small clay pot and pointed to the far corner of the garden, where mist-dew herbs clustered in shadow. 'Water them at dawn, not noon,' he said. 'I speak from *experience* — I lost a whole row my first season.' He smiled, but his eyes held the weight of that old loss. The herbs swayed gently, as if remembering it too.
experience:0.cnHint: 同门师兄将一个小陶罐交给我，凭借____告诫我要在黎明而非正午浇水。
experience:0.hook: At midnight, one mist-dew herb turned its face toward the moon and shivered.
experience:0.line: 'I speak from *experience* — I lost a whole row my first season.'

lot:0.en: Xiaoxing pulled me into the herb garden before breakfast, eyes bright. She gestured at the long wooden shelves lining the walls, each holding dozens of labeled pots. 'There is a *lot* to learn here,' she whispered, 'but Master Qingwu says each herb is a sentence waiting to be read.' I touched the nearest pot and felt a hum travel up my fingers into my chest.
lot:0.cnHint: 同门师妹带我来到灵植园，指着满架草药说这里有____需要学习。
lot:0.hook: One pot at the far end of the shelf rattled, though no wind had entered.
lot:0.line: 'There is a *lot* to learn here, but each herb is a sentence waiting to be read.'

public:0.en: Each morning the senior disciples gathered in the central garden hall for the reading of the day's herb-signs — a *public* ritual meant to teach young disciples how to read the living words around them. Master Qingwu would name each herb's current state aloud, and we would copy the sounds into our journals. Today she stopped mid-sentence and looked up at the ceiling with still eyes.
public:0.cnHint: 每天清晨，高年级弟子在灵植园中进行____仪式，共同诵读草药所示之兆。
public:0.hook: The ceiling above her had begun, very slowly, to glow green.
public:0.line: 'This *public* reading is how the garden teaches all of us at once,' Master Qingwu said.

example:0.en: Shen Wujiu crouched beside a pale blue herb and beckoned me down to his level. 'Watch how it breathes,' he said. 'This one is a perfect *example* of a word-formula taking root in living matter — see how the stem bends toward sound, not light.' I leaned close and heard, faintly, a syllable repeating inside the stem like a slow heartbeat.
example:0.cnHint: 同门师兄让我观察一株蓝色草药，称其是字诀在生命体中扎根的绝佳____。
example:0.hook: The syllable inside the stem changed — and I felt it change inside my own throat too.
example:0.line: 'This one is a perfect *example* of a word-formula taking root in living matter.'

whether:0.en: I stood at the entrance of the garden hall, journal in hand, uncertain which row to begin. Xiaoxing appeared beside me and tilted her head. 'Master Qingwu says it does not matter *whether* you start from the east row or the west,' she said gently. 'The herbs will find you either way.' As if to prove it, a bright amber plant at the far end leaned unmistakably in my direction.
whether:0.cnHint: 同门师妹告诉我，青雾师尊说____从东排还是西排开始都无关紧要，草药自会寻你。
whether:0.hook: The amber plant leaned a fraction further, and its glow touched my sleeve.
whether:0.line: 'It does not matter *whether* you start from the east row or the west — the herbs will find you.'

focus:0.en: Master Qingwu stood at the center of the garden and asked each of us to close our eyes. 'Let your *focus* settle on one scent,' she said, her voice low and even. 'Not the whole garden — just one thread of fragrance. Follow it until it forms a shape behind your eyes.' I found mine: something cool and silver, curling upward like a written character I almost recognized.
focus:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊要我们闭上眼睛，将____集中在一缕香气上，直到它在心中化为形状。
focus:0.hook: The shape behind my eyes held still for one breath — then burned bright and vanished.
focus:0.line: 'Let your *focus* settle on one scent, not the whole garden — just one thread of fragrance.'

avoid:0.en: Xiaoxing tugged my sleeve as I reached for a deep-red herb near the back wall. 'You should *avoid* that one until your second year,' she said quickly, not unkindly. 'It releases its word all at once — and if you are not ready, the sound fills your chest and you cannot speak for three days.' I withdrew my hand. The red herb pulsed once, as though it had already noticed me.
avoid:0.cnHint: 同门师妹提醒我要____碰那株深红色草药，否则释放的字诀会让人三日无法开口。
avoid:0.hook: The red herb pulsed a second time, and the air around it bent like heat above a flame.
avoid:0.line: 'You should *avoid* that herb until your second year — it releases its word all at once.'

view:0.en: The herb garden floats at the mountain's edge, open to the sky on three sides. I press my face close to a silver-leafed plant and *view* its tiny veins as if reading a secret map. Master Qingwu says each vein carries a syllable of healing. I count seven. The eighth is missing.
view:0.cnHint: 弟子在灵植园中仔细____一株银叶草，试图读懂其中隐藏的音节。
view:0.hook: Where the eighth vein should be, the leaf is cold as ice.
view:0.line: '*View* every vein before you speak the word,' said Master Qingwu, her voice very still.

social:0.en: Inside the herb garden's warm stone hall, disciples gather each morning to share what they have learned. It is a *social* ritual as old as the Sect itself — each of us naming one herb aloud so its power enters the air and blesses the rest. Today, when my turn came, I named 'calm.' The candles bent sideways as one.
social:0.cnHint: 灵植园中有一个古老的____仪式，弟子们轮流大声说出一种灵草的名字。
social:0.hook: No one could explain why all the flames leaned toward the door.
social:0.line: Shen Wujiu smiled: 'This *social* ritual has fed the garden's roots for a hundred years.'

skill:0.en: Xiaoxing moves through the rows of spirit herbs without brushing a single leaf. Transplanting them demands the *skill* of silence — hands steady, breath low, mind empty of want. She sets a violet root into dark soil and it glows faintly, accepting her. I try next. My root flickers and goes dark.
skill:0.cnHint: 小星展示了移植灵草所需的____，而叙述者的尝试却以失败告终。
skill:0.hook: The dark root is warm in my palm, as if still waiting to be convinced.
skill:0.line: '*Skill* is not force,' Xiaoxing said softly, not looking up from the soil.

job:0.en: Master Qingwu assigns each new disciple a *job* in the herb garden before any word of power is taught. Mine is to water the moongrass at the precise moment the clouds thin and pale light touches the pots. Miss the moment by a breath and the grass will not drink. I have missed it twice.
job:0.cnHint: 师尊在教授任何法术之前，先给每位新弟子安排一项____。
job:0.hook: Tonight the clouds part earlier than ever, and I am still on the wrong side of the garden.
job:0.line: 'Your *job* is simple,' Master Qingwu said, 'but simple is not easy.'

business:0.en: Shen Wujiu tells me the herb garden has its own kind of order: every plant has *business* with every other, root speaking to root beneath the soil. Touch one without care and three others feel it. I laugh at first, thinking him poetic. Then the row of firebloom turns toward me, all at once, without wind.
business:0.cnHint: 师兄解释说，灵植园中每株植物都与其他植物有着密切的____往来。
business:0.hook: The firebloom holds its turn toward me long after I stop moving.
business:0.line: Shen Wujiu said quietly: 'Disturb one plant and you disturb the *business* of them all.'

eat:0.en: A cracked spirit herb is not wasted in the Cloud Sea Sect. We *eat* the broken leaves in a thin broth each evening, and Master Qingwu says the words stored inside them pass gently into our bodies that way — slower than speaking, safer than force. Tonight the broth tastes of thunder. No one mentions it.
eat:0.cnHint: 弟子们每晚____一碗以碎灵草叶熬成的药汤，以温和的方式吸收其中的力量。
eat:0.hook: I set down my bowl and find one word already forming on my tongue, unasked.
eat:0.line: '*Eat* slowly,' Master Qingwu said, 'or the word inside will arrive before you are ready.'

healthy:0.en: Master Qingwu checks each plant in the garden the way a teacher checks a student's writing — not for beauty, but for truth. A *healthy* herb stands straight and its scent is clean, with no sweetness hiding rot. She stops at a pale green stalk, says nothing, marks it with a red thread. By morning it is gone.
healthy:0.cnHint: 师尊检查每株灵草是否____，就像老师批改学生作业一样仔细。
healthy:0.hook: The empty pot where the pale stalk stood is now filled with something dark and still.
healthy:0.line: 'A *healthy* plant will teach you more than a sick one ever could,' Master Qingwu said.

place:0.en: The seedling table is the most important *place* in the garden — here every new herb begins its life as a single word written on damp soil. I am given three seeds and told to write their names before planting. I write two correctly. The third name I have not yet learned, so I leave a blank. The soil glows where the blank is.
place:0.cnHint: 播种台是灵植园中最重要的____，新弟子在此将灵草的名字写在湿土上。
place:0.hook: That glowing blank waits for me, patient and bright, like a question that already knows its answer.
place:0.line: Xiaoxing pointed: 'This *place* is where a word becomes a living thing.'

actually:1.en: The herb garden stretched across a wide stone terrace, high above the clouds. Each plant glowed with a faint inner light. I had assumed the silver-leaf fern was ornamental, but Shen Wujiu knelt beside it and said it was *actually* the most powerful healing word in the entire sect. I touched one leaf, and warmth spread through my fingers.
actually:1.cnHint: 我以为那株银叶蕨只是装饰用的，师兄却说它____是全宗最强的疗愈灵草。
actually:1.hook: Then the leaf turned black at my touch.
actually:1.line: 'It is *actually* stronger than anything Master Qingwu grows in the upper garden.'

themselves:1.en: I walked the herb rows at dawn, mist curling around my ankles. The seedlings had no keeper that morning, yet *themselves* they stood perfectly straight, their leaves turned toward a light that did not come from the sun. Xiaoxing appeared beside me, whispering that the plants had chosen to grow without being told.
themselves:1.cnHint: 那些幼苗没有人照料，却____整齐地站立着，叶片朝向一道奇异的光。
themselves:1.hook: The light they faced had no visible source.
themselves:1.line: 'The seedlings arranged *themselves* in the shape of the oldest healing formula.'

person:1.en: Master Qingwu moved through the garden naming each herb in a low, steady voice. I had expected a distant teacher, but she was the kind of *person* who paused to let you smell every leaf before explaining its use. By the end of the row, I had already memorised five words. She smiled, then looked sharply at the sky.
person:1.cnHint: 青雾师尊是那种会让你先闻每片叶子再讲解的____，我已不知不觉记住了五个灵词。
person:1.hook: A single cloud had stopped moving above us.
person:1.line: 'Every *person* who has mastered that word began right here, in this garden.'

without:1.en: Xiaoxing could recite the name of any herb *without* looking at it, sensing each one by the warmth it gave off. She moved down the row with her eyes closed, naming them one by one, never pausing, never wrong. I tried to copy her and mistook bitter-root for sweetmoss. She laughed softly and took my hand to guide it.
without:1.cnHint: 小星闭着眼睛，____看植物就能说出每一株的名字，我却把苦根认成了甜苔。
without:1.hook: At the row's end, one plant had no warmth at all.
without:1.line: 'You must learn to feel *without* looking — the garden will not always be bright.'

among:1.en: The rarest herb in the garden was hidden *among* common greenstalk plants, its silver threads nearly invisible unless the morning light hit them at exactly the right angle. Shen Wujiu told me a disciple searched for three days before finding it. I spotted it in moments, and he went very quiet.
among:1.cnHint: 那株最稀有的灵草藏在____普通绿茎草之间，师兄说曾有弟子找了三天才找到。
among:1.hook: Shen Wujiu's silence felt heavier than any words.
among:1.line: '*Among* all the herbs here, that one chooses who may see it.'

suppose:1.en: I knelt beside a pale blue flower I did not recognise. Xiaoxing crouched next to me, tilting her head. 'I *suppose* it could be cloud-petal,' she said slowly, 'but cloud-petal never grows this far down the mountain.' We both leaned closer. The petals folded shut, as if the flower had heard us and disagreed.
suppose:1.cnHint: 小星看着那朵陌生的蓝花说，她____它可能是云瓣花，但云瓣花从不长在山腰这么低的地方。
suppose:1.hook: The closed petals began to pulse with a dim red glow.
suppose:1.line: 'I *suppose* we should tell Master Qingwu before we touch it.'

health:1.en: Master Qingwu explained that every herb in this garden was a living word for *health*, and that reading them aloud in the right order could mend a broken body as surely as any medicine. I repeated the first sequence under my breath. A small cut on my palm, earned that morning on a thorny stem, closed without a scar.
health:1.cnHint: 青雾师尊说园中每株草都是____的活字，按正确顺序朗读它们，能愈合受损的身体。
health:1.hook: But somewhere below the clouds, a bell rang once — the sect's warning bell.
health:1.line: '*Health* is not just the absence of harm — these words teach you to grow stronger.'

mean:1.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a sprig of dark violet herb and asked what I thought its name might *mean*. I studied the narrow leaves and the faint silver dust along their edges. 'Rest?' I guessed. He shook his head. 'Flight,' he said. One leaf detached, rose two inches into the still air, and stayed there.
mean:1.cnHint: 师兄问我那株深紫色灵草的名字____什么，我猜是"休息"，他却说是"飞翔"。
mean:1.hook: The hovering leaf began to drift toward the mountain's edge.
mean:1.line: 'What does it *mean* when a leaf rises on its own in a windless garden?'

derive:1.en: In the spirit herb garden, each plant held a secret name. Master Qingwu knelt beside a pale blue flower and said we could *derive* great healing power from its roots if we spoke the correct formula at dawn. I pressed my fingers into the soft soil, feeling the word take shape inside me. Somewhere above, a cloud shifted without wind.
derive:1.cnHint: 在灵植园中，师尊告诉我们可以从一株蓝花的根部____出强大的治愈之力。
derive:1.hook: The flower's petals folded shut, though the sun had not yet set.
derive:1.line: 'We can *derive* the healing word from its roots at first light.'

report:1.en: Xiaoxing handed me a folded paper at the garden gate — my first *report* from the Sect elder, written in green ink that smelled of pine and old clouds. It listed every herb I had failed to name correctly. The list was long. A single red mark sat at the bottom, shaped like an eye that would not close.
report:1.cnHint: 小星把长老写的____递给我，上面记录了我叫错名字的每一株灵草。
report:1.hook: The red mark at the bottom blinked once, then went still.
report:1.line: 'Your *report* has reached the elder — he read every word.'

research:1.en: Shen Wujiu spent three mornings in the spirit herb garden, crouching low and taking small notes on bark-paper. He called it *research*, the quiet work of learning which roots could carry a word and which would burn it away. I watched him and tried to copy his patience. The soil beneath my feet turned faintly warm.
research:1.cnHint: 师兄在灵植园里进行____，记录哪些草根能承载灵词，哪些会将其烧尽。
research:1.hook: The bark-paper curled at the edges and would not lie flat again.
research:1.line: 'This *research* may tell us why the south herbs keep refusing our words.'

author:1.en: Near the garden wall hung a stone tablet carved with formulas no one had used in a hundred years. Xiaoxing whispered that the *author* of those words had turned into wind on the day the last great peak fell into the clouds. I traced one character with my finger. The stone felt warmer than the afternoon sun could explain.
author:1.cnHint: 石碑上那些无人使用已久的灵文，其____据说在最后一座山峰沉入云海时化为了风。
author:1.hook: Under my finger, the carved character began to glow a faint, restless gold.
author:1.line: 'The *author* of these formulas left no name — only the words themselves.'

increase:1.en: Master Qingwu told us that speaking a plant's true name would *increase* its healing power by exactly as much as the speaker's sincerity. Shen Wujiu spoke first — the herb in his hand grew three new leaves in a breath. I tried and managed one small leaf, trembling at its edge. Above us, the mountain hummed.
increase:1.cnHint: 师尊说，说出灵草的真名能____其治愈之力，增幅取决于说话者的诚意。
increase:1.hook: The single leaf on my herb turned silver at its tip before the hum faded.
increase:1.line: 'Speak with full heart and you will *increase* the herb's power threefold.'

university:1.en: Before I came here, I studied at a small *university* on a low hill where nothing floated and no word ever healed a wound. Master Qingwu said that learning is the same in every place — slow, stubborn, and worth it. I believed her, mostly. In the garden, a seed I had planted last week finally split open, pushing one green shoot toward the open sky.
university:1.cnHint: 加入云海宗之前，我曾在山下的一所____读书，那里没有灵草，没有能治愈伤口的灵词。
university:1.hook: The green shoot pointed not toward the sun but toward the highest, hidden peak.
university:1.line: 'My old *university* taught me words, but not how to make them live.'

turn:1.en: Xiaoxing showed me how to *turn* a dried root slowly between both palms while speaking its name — the warmth of the hands would wake the word inside. I tried three times. On the third, the root began to glow, and the glow traveled up my wrists like slow fire. Shen Wujiu stepped back without a word. His shadow fell the wrong way.
turn:1.cnHint: 小星教我如何在双掌间慢慢____一截干根，用掌心的温度唤醒其中的灵词。
turn:1.hook: Shen Wujiu's shadow stretched toward the east, though the sun stood in the west.
turn:1.line: '*Turn* it slowly — the word inside wakes only when it feels patient hands.'

end:1.en: The herb garden stretches along the edge of the floating mountain, row after row of glowing leaves. I walk each path slowly, learning every plant by name. At the *end* of the last row stands a single black stem with no leaves at all — only a faint hum, like a word not yet spoken.
end:1.cnHint: 灵植园的小径尽头，有一株奇异的黑茎植物静静伫立，发出低沉的嗡鸣。
end:1.hook: No one had told me that stem was not supposed to be there.
end:1.line: 'Walk to the *end* of the row and stop — do not touch the black stem,' said Shen Wujiu.

important:1.en: Master Qingwu moves through the herb garden without hurrying, touching each plant the way one touches a sleeping child. She stops beside a pale silver fern. 'This one,' she says quietly, 'is the most *important* herb in the garden.' Above us, the sky begins to darken at its edges, though it is still midday.
important:1.cnHint: 师尊在灵植园中向弟子指出最____的一株草药，话音未落，天色忽然暗了。
important:1.hook: The silver fern shivered, though there was no wind.
important:1.line: 'Remember, the most *important* herb is often the one that looks weakest,' said Master Qingwu.

cause:1.en: Xiaoxing shows me which herbs grow in pairs — each one needs its neighbor to stay alive. If you remove one, she explains, the other will wither within a day. Careless hands can *cause* the whole row to fail. She says this gently, but her eyes drift to a gap in the soil where a plant is already missing.
cause:1.cnHint: 同门师妹解释，随意采摘某株草药会____整排植物枯萎，而园中已有一处空缺。
cause:1.hook: The gap in the soil was perfectly round, as if something had been pulled out from below.
cause:1.line: 'Even one wrong step can *cause* the rarest herb to die,' Xiaoxing said softly.

accord:1.en: Each herb in the garden hums at its own pitch, Shen Wujiu tells me. When the garden is healthy, all the hums rise and fall in *accord*, like voices in a quiet song. I close my eyes and listen. The harmony is almost perfect — almost. One low note pulls slightly away from the rest.
accord:1.cnHint: 同门师兄说，健康的灵植园中每株草药的嗡鸣声应彼此____，但今日有一个音调悄悄偏离了。
accord:1.hook: The discordant note grew louder each time I turned my back.
accord:1.line: 'When every herb grows in *accord*, the garden can heal even a broken spirit,' said Shen Wujiu.

result:1.en: I try mixing two herb powders the way Xiaoxing showed me, grinding them in the stone bowl until the color shifts from green to pale gold. The *result* is a fine dust that smells of rain and pine. Xiaoxing nods, then points to a dark vein running through the gold — something I did not put there.
result:1.cnHint: 我按照师妹所教研磨两种草药，____是一捧金色细粉，但其中却有一道不该出现的暗纹。
result:1.hook: The dark vein pulsed once, then lay still.
result:1.line: 'The *result* of this mix should be pure gold — never dark,' said Xiaoxing, frowning.

recent:1.en: Shen Wujiu kneels by a cluster of herbs near the garden wall and brushes the soil with two fingers. He says that the roots show signs of *recent* movement — not by wind, not by rain, but by something deliberate. He stands slowly and looks toward the inner mountain path without speaking.
recent:1.cnHint: 同门师兄发现园中一丛草药的根部有____被动过的痕迹，并非风雨所为，似乎出自某种刻意为之。
recent:1.hook: The inner path was supposed to be sealed after last night's bell.
recent:1.line: 'These marks are *recent* — made no more than one night ago,' Shen Wujiu said quietly.

start:1.en: Master Qingwu hands me a small empty jar and tells me today I will harvest my first herb alone. My fingers tremble at the *start*, unsure which leaves to take and which to leave. But the plant seems to lean toward me, just slightly, as if offering itself. When I look up, Master Qingwu is already gone.
start:1.cnHint: 师尊交给我一只空瓶，让我独自采药；____时我的手在颤抖，却感觉那株草药微微向我倾身。
start:1.hook: The jar was warm in my hand, warmer than the afternoon sun could explain.
start:1.line: 'At the *start* of every harvest, breathe once and let the herb come to you,' said Master Qingwu.

however:1.en: The garden looks peaceful from the path — neat rows, soft light, the smell of green things growing. *However*, when I step between the rows, the air changes. It thickens, presses gently against my ears. Xiaoxing said I would feel this, but she did not say it would feel like being watched.
however:1.cnHint: 灵植园从小径望去一片祥和，____一旦踏入其间，空气便变得厚重，仿佛有目光追随着你。
however:1.hook: When I turned to leave, the rows behind me had shifted.
however:1.line: 'The garden looks still, *however*, it listens to every word you speak,' Xiaoxing warned.

less:1.en: The spirit herb garden stretched across the narrow ridge, every plant humming with quiet power. Master Qingwu walked the rows slowly, pinching dead leaves. 'Tend *less* to the outer ring,' she said, 'and give your care to what grows at the centre.' I knelt and pressed my fingers into the warm soil. Above us, the clouds thinned, and one pale star appeared before dusk.
less:1.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诉我，对外围的草药花____时间，把心思放在中心。
less:1.hook: The star should not have risen this early.
less:1.line: 'Give *less* water to the edges — the heart roots drink first.'

information:1.en: Shen Wujiu spread a worn chart over the garden wall, weighing its corners with smooth stones. Each symbol on the paper held *information* about which herb needed shade and which needed open sky. I copied every mark into my own small notebook, hand trembling slightly. The wind shifted, and the whole sea of clouds below us rolled once, like a slow breath.
information:1.cnHint: 师兄展开图表，里面包含关于每株灵草的重要____。
information:1.hook: Then the chart's ink began to glow faint green.
information:1.line: 'This single mark carries *information* three seasons of failure taught me.'

paragraph:1.en: Master Qingwu handed me an old text and asked me to read aloud. The third *paragraph* described how speaking a healing word over wounded bark could close a split branch in minutes. I read it twice, then pressed my palm to a cracked stem nearby. Warmth moved through my fingers. Somewhere deep in the mountain, stone groaned.
paragraph:1.cnHint: 师尊让我朗读古籍，其中第三____描述了如何用语言治愈受伤的草木。
paragraph:1.hook: The groaning did not stop when my voice did.
paragraph:1.line: 'Read that *paragraph* again — slower this time, and mean it.'

look:1.en: Xiaoxing crouched beside a silver-leafed plant and gave me a careful *look*, the kind that carries a warning. 'Do not touch the grey stem before noon,' she whispered. I pulled my hand back just in time. The plant's leaves folded shut on their own, as if they had sensed my doubt. A thin mist rose from the soil and hung at knee height.
look:1.cnHint: 小星给了我一个意味深长的____，示意我不要触碰那株灰茎植物。
look:1.hook: The mist rose higher and took the shape of a hand.
look:1.line: 'That *look* on your face tells me you almost touched it.'

benefit:1.en: Shen Wujiu explained that tending the spirit herbs was not only a chore — there was real *benefit* for us disciples too. Every hour spent among the living plants sharpened the mind and steadied the breath, making our own words of power clearer. I felt it already: my thoughts were quieter here than anywhere else in the Sect. Then the oldest herb in the row turned black overnight.
benefit:1.cnHint: 师兄解释说，照料灵草对我们弟子也有真正的____，能让心神更加清明。
benefit:1.hook: Nothing in the garden had ever turned black before.
benefit:1.line: 'The true *benefit* is not the harvest — it is what the plants teach your breath.'

contain:1.en: The sealed clay jar near the garden gate was said to *contain* a word so strong it could split stone if spoken aloud. Master Qingwu kept the stopper tied with red cord and never explained more. I walked past it every morning, feeling a faint vibration against my ribs. Today the red cord lay on the ground, untied, though no one had been near.
contain:1.cnHint: 院门旁的封泥罐据说____着一个能劈石的强大字符，今天红绳却松落在地。
contain:1.hook: The stopper was still in place — but barely.
contain:1.line: 'That jar must *contain* its word until the mountain calls for it.'

direction:1.en: I lost the path between the herb rows and stood still, unsure which way to go. Xiaoxing appeared from the mist and offered quiet *direction*, pointing first to the moss on the stones and then to the lean of the tallest plant. 'They all point toward the peak,' she said with a small smile. I nodded, grateful. Behind her, a cloud rose straight up like smoke from a fire.
direction:1.cnHint: 我在药圃迷路，小星给了我____，告诉我苔藓和植物都指向山顶。
direction:1.hook: Clouds do not rise that way unless something burns below.
direction:1.line: 'When you are lost, ask the herbs — they always know the *direction* of the peak.'

attach:1.en: Master Qingwu showed me how to *attach* a written word-charm to the stem of a weak herb using nothing but morning dew and breath. The tiny strip of bark held firm, and within moments the drooping leaves lifted. I practiced on three plants before the lesson ended. When I looked up, every charm I had placed was glowing, and they were all glowing the same deep gold at once.
attach:1.cnHint: 师尊教我用晨露和气息将字符____在虚弱的灵草茎上，为其注入生机。
attach:1.hook: Gold light meant mastery — but I had only just begun.
attach:1.line: '*Attach* the charm gently — force will crack the stem and silence the word.'

likely:1.en: The garden of spirit herbs stretched across the southern edge of our floating mountain. Each plant held a single word inside its leaves. Shen Wujiu pointed to a pale green shoot near the stone wall. 'That one is *likely* to bloom before dawn,' he said. 'Pick it then, and the word inside will be clear and strong.' I knelt beside it, waiting.
likely:1.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，那株灵草____在黎明前开花，那时采摘效果最佳。
likely:1.hook: But the shoot had already begun to wither at its root.
likely:1.line: 'That herb is *likely* to give you your first real word if you tend it well.'

experience:1.en: Master Qingwu walked slowly between the rows of spirit herbs, touching none of them. She paused at a withered stalk and closed her eyes. 'Every plant you lose is still part of your *experience*,' she said. 'The sect does not measure disciples by what grows, but by what they learn from what dies.' I wrote that into my memory like ink into stone.
experience:1.cnHint: 师尊说，每一次失败都是____的一部分，门派看重的是从中学到的东西。
experience:1.hook: Then she opened her eyes and looked not at the herb, but at me.
experience:1.line: 'Your *experience* here in this garden will shape every word you ever speak.'

lot:1.en: Xiaoxing had been assigned the eastern beds, where the rarest herbs grew in shallow soil. She had tended them for three weeks without rest. When I arrived to help, I saw that a *lot* of the young plants had already taken root and were beginning to glow faintly at the leaf edges. She smiled without pride. 'They just needed someone to believe in them,' she said.
lot:1.cnHint: 小星照料的东边花圃里，____灵草已经扎根，叶缘开始散发微光。
lot:1.hook: Yet one bed at the far end remained dark and completely still.
lot:1.line: 'A *lot* of these herbs were nearly dead when I found them — now look at them glow.'

public:1.en: The mid-year recitation was a *public* ceremony held on the open stone platform at the mountain's highest point, where all disciples and their masters gathered beneath the open sky. I stood before them and spoke a single word I had harvested from the herb garden. It rose from my lips like smoke and formed a small bright shape in the air. The crowd went silent.
public:1.cnHint: 在山顶的____仪式上，我念出从灵植园采下的那个词，它化作光形浮在空中。
public:1.hook: The shape hung there one breath too long before it cracked apart.
public:1.line: 'In this *public* ceremony, every word you speak becomes part of the sect's record.'

example:1.en: Shen Wujiu pulled a single leaf from a silver-stemmed herb and held it to the light. Inside it, a word glowed like an ember. 'This is the best *example* I can give you of what a perfectly stored word looks like,' he said. 'Notice the even light — no dark edges, no trembling.' I held my own leaf beside his. Mine trembled at every edge.
example:1.cnHint: 师兄用一片完美的叶子作为____，教我辨别一个词是否被妥善封存其中。
example:1.hook: A cold wind crossed the garden, and both leaves flickered at once.
example:1.line: 'Let this leaf be your *example* — study the light inside it before you try your own.'

whether:1.en: I stood before two herbs that looked almost the same. One held a word for healing; the other held a word for wind. Master Qingwu had not told me which was which. I had to decide *whether* to trust the faint warmth in my palm or the faint scent in the air. I chose warmth. I reached for the left herb, broke its stem, and waited to see if I had chosen well.
whether:1.cnHint: 面对两株相似的灵草，我必须判断____该凭手心的温度还是空气中的气味来选择。
whether:1.hook: The word that rose from the broken stem was neither healing nor wind.
whether:1.line: 'You must decide *whether* to trust your hand or your nose — both can mislead you here.'

focus:1.en: The spirit herbs in the northern bed required absolute stillness to tend. A scattered mind would cause them to close their leaves and seal the words inside too tightly to harvest. Xiaoxing showed me how to narrow my breath, to let the *focus* of my attention rest on one plant at a time like sunlight through still water. When I tried it, the nearest leaf opened slowly toward me.
focus:1.cnHint: 小星教我将注意力的____集中在一株灵草上，心神涣散会让它封闭叶片。
focus:1.hook: Three rows away, a plant I had not touched began to tremble on its own.
focus:1.line: 'Keep your *focus* on one herb at a time — these plants know when your mind has wandered.'

avoid:1.en: Master Qingwu marked the western corner of the garden with a ring of grey stones. 'You must *avoid* the herbs that grow inside that ring,' she said, her voice calm and without fear. 'They hold words that are not ready, and an unready word taken too soon will speak itself before you can shape it.' I memorized the boundary. I would not cross it. Not yet.
avoid:1.cnHint: 师尊用石圈划出禁区，叮嘱我____采摘其中尚未成熟的灵草。
avoid:1.hook: That night I heard a word — low and shapeless — drifting out from the grey stones.
avoid:1.line: '*Avoid* the grey ring entirely until I tell you those herbs are ready to be touched.'

view:1.en: The herb garden clings to the edge of the floating mountain, and from here the *view* stretches without end — pale cloud below, pale sky above, and somewhere between them, other peaks like green islands. I press a fresh leaf to my palm and feel the word inside it hum. Master Qingwu says every word holds a world if you look long enough.
view:1.cnHint: 弟子在灵植园边缘眺望云海，感受到草叶中字灵的震动，师尊曾说每个____都藏着一方天地。
view:1.hook: Then the clouds parted, and something vast moved beneath them.
view:1.line: 'The *view* from this ledge has broken stronger disciples than you,' said Master Qingwu, without turning.

social:1.en: New disciples gather each dawn in the herb garden to trade seeds and share the names of plants they have learned. Shen Wujiu calls it a *social* ritual, as necessary as watering. I watch the easy way words pass between them and feel my own mouth go quiet. I have not yet earned a word worth trading.
social:1.cnHint: 清晨，弟子们在灵植园进行____交流，互换草药名讳，师兄说这是必要的修行仪式。
social:1.hook: Behind the laughter, one disciple's eyes never left me.
social:1.line: 'A *social* habit among disciples keeps the sect's roots from rotting,' Shen Wujiu said, pressing a seed into my hand.

skill:1.en: Xiaoxing kneels beside a row of silver-leafed herbs, her fingers moving with a *skill* I cannot copy — one touch to know the word inside, one breath to draw it out whole. She learned this in her first month. I am in my third, and still I bruise every leaf I press. The garden records each failure in wilted stems.
skill:1.cnHint: 师妹采摘草药时展现出高超的____，一触便知灵字，而我至今仍在损毁叶片。
skill:1.hook: A single black stem appeared overnight where her best plant had stood.
skill:1.line: '*Skill* without patience is just speed,' Xiaoxing said softly, lifting a perfect leaf, 'and speed breaks things.'

job:1.en: Each disciple is given a *job* in the herb garden when they arrive: weeding, watering, cataloguing, or guard duty at the outer ledge. Mine is to read aloud the names of growing herbs each morning so the plants can hear the words they carry. It sounds simple. Three herbs have gone silent since I began.
job:1.cnHint: 每位弟子在灵植园都有指定的____，我的任务是为草药诵读其灵名，但已有三株陷入沉默。
job:1.hook: This morning, a fourth herb turned its face away from my voice.
job:1.line: 'Your *job* is not to sing well,' said Master Qingwu, 'it is to mean what you say.'

business:1.en: A trading elder from a lower peak arrives once a month to exchange rare seeds for written words. Shen Wujiu handles all the *business* at the garden gate, calm and exact, never giving a word whose power he has not verified himself. I watch from behind a wall of tall grass and wonder what a word of mine might one day be worth.
business:1.cnHint: 下层山峰的长老月月前来以种子换灵字，师兄主持这一____，从不交出未经验证的字灵。
business:1.hook: This time the elder left two seeds behind and would not say why.
business:1.line: '*Business* at this gate moves slowly,' Shen Wujiu told the elder, 'because we only trade what is true.'

eat:1.en: Some herbs in the garden are not grown but read — their words dissolve on the tongue like morning frost. To *eat* such a word is to take its meaning into your body, and for a breath you can feel what the plant feels: deep root, slow light, patient green. Xiaoxing says the sensation fades faster each time. You must hold it before it goes.
eat:1.cnHint: 有些灵草的字灵可被____入体，使人短暂感受草木之心，师妹说这感觉会越来越短暂。
eat:1.hook: One word I swallowed this morning left a taste I could not name by evening.
eat:1.line: 'Do not *eat* a word you cannot yet read clearly,' Xiaoxing warned, brushing soil from her sleeve, 'or it will read you instead.'

healthy:1.en: Master Qingwu walks the rows each week, pressing her palm flat against the soil. A *healthy* patch of ground glows faintly under her hand — the words below the surface still alive and feeding the roots above. She paused today at the far corner where I water each morning, and her hand did not glow. She said nothing and walked on.
healthy:1.cnHint: 师尊每周巡视灵植园，____的土地在她手下会微微发光，今日她停在我负责的那片土地前，手中却没有光。
healthy:1.hook: She paused once at the gate and looked back at that dark corner.
healthy:1.line: 'A *healthy* garden remembers every word ever spoken inside it,' Master Qingwu said, not looking at me.

place:1.en: The oldest corner of the herb garden is called the Still *Place* — no wind reaches it, no cloud shadow crosses it, and the herbs there grow without names because no one has been able to read them yet. Disciples are told not to linger. But this afternoon I heard a sound from inside it, low and rhythmic, like a word being said very slowly by something that has waited a long time to speak.
place:1.cnHint: 灵植园最古老的角落被称为静____，那里的草药尚无灵名，弟子们被告知不可久留，但今日我听见了声音。
place:1.hook: The sound stopped the moment I turned to walk away.
place:1.line: 'This *place* holds words older than the sect,' Shen Wujiu said quietly, pulling me back from the edge.

derive:2.en: In the herb garden, I found a hollow stone with a folded note inside. The note listed rare roots and their positions among the beds. Master Qingwu had taught us that a healer must *derive* strength from the land itself, reading each plant as a living word. The stone hummed faintly.
derive:2.cnHint: 我在灵植园的空心石中发现一张字条，说明如何从大地____力量。
derive:2.hook: The stone was warm, as if someone had just left it.
derive:2.line: 'We *derive* our power from what the earth freely gives,' said Master Qingwu.

report:2.en: Near the eastern beds, a rolled leaf sealed with wax lay against a root marker. I broke the seal and unfolded it: a *report* on three herbs that had wilted overnight, written in Shen Wujiu's careful hand. Numbers, dates, and small drawings of leaves filled every line. Something had drained them.
report:2.cnHint: 师兄在灵植园写了一份关于三株枯萎灵草的____，交到了我手中。
report:2.hook: All three herbs grew in a perfect, silent circle.
report:2.line: 'This *report* shows the herbs lost their glow before midnight,' said Shen Wujiu.

research:2.en: Tucked beneath the oldest ginkgo in the garden was a worn journal. Its pages were dense with pressed petals and tiny notes. Xiaoxing said Master Qingwu had spent ten years in silent *research* here, learning which herbs could mend a broken spirit. The journal smelled of rain and deep time.
research:2.cnHint: 小星告诉我，师尊曾在此处进行多年的____，留下了一本古旧笔记。
research:2.hook: The last page had been torn out cleanly.
research:2.line: 'His *research* began long before any of us arrived,' said Xiaoxing softly.

different:2.en: Shen Wujiu led me down a side path I had never noticed. The herbs here stood taller, their colors *different* from those in the main beds — deep violet instead of pale green, leaves curved like open palms. He said nothing, only watched my face as I read the small wooden sign beside them.
different:2.cnHint: 师兄带我来到一条小径，这里的灵草与主圃____，颜色深紫，令我驻足。
different:2.hook: The wooden sign bore a name I could not yet read.
different:2.line: 'These are *different* — do not touch them without permission,' Shen Wujiu warned.

author:2.en: Half-buried in the soft soil near the lotus pool, I uncovered a flat stone tablet. Carved words covered its face: a list of herb names and their hidden uses. At the bottom, a single character marked the *author* of the text. I did not know the name, but Master Qingwu had gone very still.
author:2.cnHint: 莲池旁的石碑刻满灵草名录，碑底刻有____的名字，令师尊神色一变。
author:2.hook: Master Qingwu's hand paused just above the carved name.
author:2.line: 'The *author* of this tablet has not walked here for a hundred years,' said Master Qingwu.

increase:2.en: Xiaoxing showed me two beds side by side. One had been treated with a new mineral water drawn from the lower springs; the other had not. The treated herbs stood nearly twice as tall. 'The mineral water causes a clear *increase* in their growth,' she said, pointing to the roots with quiet pride.
increase:2.cnHint: 小星指着两块对比苗床，展示泉水处理后灵草____的效果。
increase:2.hook: Yet the taller herbs cast no shadow at all.
increase:2.line: 'The *increase* happened in a single night — I measured it myself,' said Xiaoxing.

university:2.en: Inside the seed vault at the garden's edge, I found a bronze plaque. It named this vault as a gift from the Cloud Sea *University* of Spiritual Arts, founded three centuries ago. Master Qingwu had studied there before the school closed. The plaque was cold, though the air around it was warm.
university:2.cnHint: 种子库的铜牌显示，这里是一所古老____赠予本门的礼物。
university:2.hook: The school had closed the same year Master Qingwu left.
university:2.line: 'That *university* shaped every healer in this sect,' said Master Qingwu quietly.

turn:2.en: I was pressing a cutting into fresh soil when the whole garden seemed to *turn* — not the ground, but the light. Shadows swung east as if noon had skipped to dusk in a breath. Shen Wujiu looked up sharply. Every herb in the eastern bed had opened its leaves and then closed them again.
turn:2.cnHint: 我在扦插时，园中光线忽然____，东侧灵草齐齐开合了一次叶片。
turn:2.hook: Shen Wujiu whispered: 'It has begun counting.'
turn:2.line: 'Watch the light *turn* — the garden is trying to tell us something,' said Shen Wujiu.

less:2.en: The spirit herb garden held hundreds of living words, each leaf a whispered lesson. Shen Wujiu handed me a small clay pot. 'This one needs *less* water than the others,' he said, 'or its meaning grows bitter.' I measured carefully. The herb glowed a soft green — then, without warning, one petal turned grey.
less:2.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，这株灵草需要____的水分，否则药性会变苦。
less:2.hook: The grey petal fell, and the soil beneath it spelled a warning.
less:2.line: 'This plant needs *less* light, or it will forget its own name.'

information:2.en: Tucked beneath a stone in the garden I found a folded leaf. Pressed into it, in tiny root-strokes, was *information* about a herb that had not been cultivated for three generations. My fingers tingled as I read. Outside the garden wall, a wind rose from nowhere and scattered the seed pods of every nearby plant.
information:2.cnHint: 我在石头下找到一片叶子，上面记载着关于一株失传灵草的____。
information:2.hook: The last line of the leaf read: 'Do not read this alone at dusk.'
information:2.line: 'This *information* was sealed away for a reason — read it carefully.'

paragraph:2.en: Master Qingwu set a moss-covered tablet before me in the garden. 'Copy the third *paragraph*,' she said, 'exactly as it stands.' The words wriggled like roots seeking water. When I finished copying, the tablet cracked cleanly down the middle, releasing a scent like rain on warm stone.
paragraph:2.cnHint: 师尊让我抄写石碑上第三____的内容，抄完后石碑裂开了。
paragraph:2.hook: From the crack, a single seedling pushed up — one no one had planted.
paragraph:2.line: 'Read the third *paragraph* aloud only when the clouds are still.'

look:2.en: Xiaoxing caught my sleeve near the moonpetal row. 'Give it a proper *look* before you touch anything,' she urged, pointing at a vine whose leaves faced downward — a sign of hidden tension in the root-words below. I stepped back and studied it. A low hum rose from the soil, steady as a held breath.
look:2.cnHint: 师妹提醒我，在触碰任何灵草之前，先仔细____一遍。
look:2.hook: The hum stopped the moment I reached out my hand.
look:2.line: 'Take a careful *look* — some words here bite if you rush them.'

benefit:2.en: Shen Wujiu showed me how to press two herbs together so each one could *benefit* from the other's stored warmth. The weaker plant straightened within moments, its word-vein brightening like ink meeting water. I smiled — then noticed the shadow of a large bird cross the garden, though the sky above held no bird at all.
benefit:2.cnHint: 师兄教我将两株灵草合在一起，让它们彼此____，弱小的那株迅速恢复了生机。
benefit:2.hook: The shadow circled once, then pointed, like a finger, toward the eastern peak.
benefit:2.line: 'Let them grow side by side — each will *benefit* from the other's strength.'

contain:2.en: One clay jar in the corner of the garden was sealed with wax and cord. A label in Master Qingwu's hand read: 'This vessel must *contain* the night-root at all times — open only in full daylight.' The wax was cracked. I pressed it closed with both palms, and the jar shook once, very gently, against my hands.
contain:2.cnHint: 角落里有一只封口的陶罐，标签写着它必须____某种夜根，我发现封蜡已经裂开。
contain:2.hook: From beneath the sealed lid came one slow, deliberate knock.
contain:2.line: 'These words are wild — this jar must *contain* them until we are ready.'

direction:2.en: The garden paths crossed at the centre in a star of seven routes. Xiaoxing studied the soil at each crossing, reading the root-marks. 'The herbs grow in the *direction* of the strongest formula,' she explained. All seven paths leaned east today — all except one, which bent sharply toward a patch of bare, dark earth no one could explain.
direction:2.cnHint: 师妹说，灵草生长的____会指向最强的法阵，但有一条路指向了一片无人能解释的黑土。
direction:2.hook: That bare patch had not been there yesterday morning.
direction:2.line: 'Follow the *direction* the roots lean — they know things the maps do not.'

attach:2.en: Master Qingwu showed me how to *attach* a small written word-seal to the stem of a new cutting so it would remember its original mountain. Without the seal, she said, the herb forgets its nature within a day. I tied mine with careful fingers. As I stepped back, all the seals in the garden rustled at once, as though stirred by the same unseen breath.
attach:2.cnHint: 师尊教我如何将一枚字印____在新插条的茎上，让它记住自己来自哪座山。
attach:2.hook: Every seal in the garden faced the same direction — toward the sealed eastern gate.

actually:2.en: The herb garden stretched across a narrow shelf of rock, high above the clouds. Each plant glowed faintly, as if breathing. I had expected silence, but the air hummed with soft voices — the herbs were *actually* speaking to one another in a language older than any scroll. I pressed my ear close and heard my own name.
actually:2.cnHint: 弟子在灵植园发现草药们____在彼此交谈，甚至提到了自己的名字。
actually:2.hook: And the oldest root turned slowly toward me.
actually:2.line: 'They are *actually* alive in a way no text ever told us.'

themselves:2.en: Master Qingwu led me through the upper garden at dawn. The rarest herbs, she said, had learned to tend *themselves* — trimming dead leaves, turning toward light, sealing their own wounds with silver sap. I watched a small blue fern fold and unfold like a breathing chest. No hand had ever touched it.
themselves:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诉弟子，最珍贵的灵草能够____照料自己，无需人手。
themselves:2.hook: Then every fern in the row turned to face the same dark corner.
themselves:2.line: 'These herbs have learned to heal *themselves* without any help from us.'

person:2.en: A folded note lay tucked beneath a silver-leafed plant near the garden wall. The handwriting was careful and old. It said only: seek the *person* who planted the first seed. I looked up at the mountain above us, where no disciple was allowed to go, and saw a single light moving.
person:2.cnHint: 弟子在灵植园发现一张纸条，指引他去寻找某个____。
person:2.hook: The light paused, as if it knew it was being watched.
person:2.line: 'Every disciple here owes a debt to the *person* who first grew these herbs.'

without:2.en: Shen Wujiu showed me how to harvest the golden root. The trick, he said, was to lift it *without* breaking the thin threads beneath — those threads fed the whole row. I was careful. I was slow. Still, one thread snapped, and the row shivered as one, every leaf going pale at the same moment.
without:2.cnHint: 沈无咎示范如何在____折断细根的情况下采集灵草，但弟子还是失手了。
without:2.hook: A faint groan rose from the soil below.
without:2.line: 'You must lift the root *without* touching those lower threads — not once.'

among:2.en: Xiaoxing knelt *among* the smallest herbs at the garden's edge, each one no taller than a finger. She was whispering something to them, and they were leaning in, the way students lean toward a teacher. I had thought she was only a junior disciple. I began to wonder what she truly was.
among:2.cnHint: 弟子发现小星____那些最矮小的灵草之间低语，草儿们纷纷向她倾身。
among:2.hook: When she stood, every small herb had turned a deeper shade of green.
among:2.line: 'I always feel most calm *among* the smallest and quietest ones.'

suppose:2.en: I found a root I did not recognise — deep red, shaped like a closed hand. I *suppose* it could have been harmless, but the soil around it was grey and dry in a ring, as if the root had drawn all life inward. I set my basket down. I did not pick it. I went to find Master Qingwu instead.
suppose:2.cnHint: 弟子发现一株奇异的红色灵根，____它可能无害，但四周土壤已然枯死。
suppose:2.hook: Behind me, the red root slowly opened.
suppose:2.line: 'I *suppose* we should not touch anything we cannot name first.'

health:2.en: The jade board at the garden gate listed each herb by its use: breath, bone, memory, sleep. At the bottom, in the oldest script, one entry read simply — *health* of the mountain itself. I had never thought of the mountain as a living thing. Now, standing on its edge, I felt it breathe beneath my feet.
health:2.cnHint: 园门玉牌记录着每株灵草的用途，最后一条写着维护山体本身的____。
health:2.hook: Then the mountain exhaled, and the clouds below rose three feet.
health:2.line: 'Without these herbs the *health* of our whole mountain would slowly fade.'

mean:2.en: A carved mark on the oldest tree in the garden stopped me. Shen Wujiu said such marks *mean* that a master once sealed something inside — a word, a warning, or a piece of their own spirit. The bark over the mark was warm to the touch, even in the cold morning air. I pulled my hand back slowly.
mean:2.cnHint: 沈无咎解释说，古树上的刻痕____着曾有师长在此封印了某种东西。
mean:2.hook: Under my palm, the mark had begun to glow.
mean:2.line: 'Those signs *mean* someone hid a living formula inside the wood.'

end:2.en: The herb garden stretched along the mountain's edge, each plant glowing faintly in the morning mist. I walked the long path between the rows until I reached the *end*, where a single silver-leafed plant stood apart from all the others, untouched and wrapped in a thin curl of cloud. No disciple had recorded it in any scroll.
end:2.cnHint: 我走到灵植园小径的____，发现了一株从未被记录过的银叶灵草。
end:2.hook: The silver leaves trembled, though the air was perfectly still.
end:2.line: 'At the *end* of the path,' Shen Wujiu said, 'only the bravest disciples ever look.'

important:2.en: Xiaoxing pressed a folded note into my hand before dawn, her voice barely above a whisper. The note held a single word-formula I had never seen in any lesson. She said knowing it was *important*, more than any herb we had studied that week, because it was the only word that could seal a broken root-vein. I kept it close all morning.
important:2.cnHint: 小星告诉我，这个字诀非常____，因为它能封住断裂的根脉。
important:2.hook: By midday the note had begun to glow faintly warm against my palm.
important:2.line: 'This word is *important*,' Xiaoxing said, 'do not let it leave your hand before nightfall.'

cause:2.en: A cluster of red-thorn herbs near the garden wall had wilted overnight. Shen Wujiu knelt beside them, studying the soil with careful eyes. He told me that a single wrong formula, spoken too close to a living root, could *cause* the whole row to lose its spiritual force within hours. I looked at the dry earth and felt the weight of every word I had ever said carelessly.
cause:2.cnHint: 师兄说，念错咒文会____一整排灵草在数小时内失去灵力。
cause:2.hook: At the far end of the row, a second cluster had already begun to turn pale.
cause:2.line: 'Careless words *cause* more harm here,' Shen Wujiu said, 'than any storm that blows off the mountain.'

accord:2.en: Master Qingwu set two bowls of soil side by side on the garden table. One held a common herb; the other held the rare silver-leaf I had found. She explained that a formula only works when its sound is in *accord* with the nature of the plant receiving it — a mismatch would push the herb's spirit inward until it collapsed. I recited the test tone, and both plants leaned, ever so slightly, toward my voice.
accord:2.cnHint: 师尊说，咒文的音调必须与灵草的本性保持____，否则灵草的灵魂会向内收缩。
accord:2.hook: The silver-leaf then leaned a small measure further than the common herb, as if it wanted more.
accord:2.line: 'Your voice must be in *accord* with the root,' Master Qingwu said, 'or the herb will refuse you entirely.'

result:2.en: I spent the morning trying to coax a slow-growing root-herb with a warming formula. By noon I checked the soil and found the roots had doubled in length overnight. Xiaoxing clapped softly and told me the *result* proved my breath-control had finally reached the first level. A faint golden line appeared along the underside of each leaf, which none of us had expected.
result:2.cnHint: 我用温热咒文催发灵根，检查土壤后发现____令人惊喜，叶片下方还浮现出金线。
result:2.hook: The golden lines began, very slowly, to spell a shape none of us recognised.
result:2.line: 'The *result* you see,' Xiaoxing said softly, 'means your breath has crossed a threshold it cannot uncross.'

recent:2.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a thin record-scroll and told me to read the *recent* entries first. The last three notes, written in Master Qingwu's careful hand, described a herb that had flowered twice in one week — something that had not happened on this mountain in living memory. The ink on the final entry was still faintly damp, as though it had been written only minutes before dawn.
recent:2.cnHint: 师兄让我先读记录卷轴上____的条目，师尊的笔迹描述了一株一周内开了两次花的灵草。
recent:2.hook: Below the last entry, a single pressed petal had been placed — still faintly warm to the touch.
recent:2.line: 'The *recent* entries,' Shen Wujiu told me, 'will unsettle you more than the old ones ever did.'

start:2.en: At the garden's entrance stood a stone marker carved with the first formula every disciple must learn. Master Qingwu said all cultivation has a *start*, and this stone was ours — the single word from which every later skill would grow like a branch from one deep root. I pressed my fingers to the carving and felt a low hum travel up through my wrist into my shoulder.
start:2.cnHint: 师尊说，所有修炼都有一个____，这块石碑上的咒文正是我们每位弟子的根基。
start:2.hook: The hum did not stop when I lifted my hand from the stone.
start:2.line: 'Every long path has a *start*,' Master Qingwu said, 'and yours has already begun to pull you forward.'

however:2.en: The morning rain had fed every herb in the garden, and each row gleamed with fresh color. I expected an easy day of quiet study. *However*, when I reached the far corner, I found a circle of ash where three rare moon-root plants had stood the evening before — no trace of soil, no fallen leaf, only the clean grey ring and a smell like burnt silk rising into the mist.
however:2.cnHint: 我以为今天会是轻松的学习日，____，角落里三株月根灵草的位置只剩下一圈灰烬。
however:2.hook: At the centre of the ash ring, a single seed rested, perfectly white and perfectly dry.
however:2.line: 'The garden looked peaceful,' Xiaoxing murmured, '*however*, something moved through it before we woke.'

human:2.en: In the spirit herb garden, a stone tablet listed every plant by its effect on the *human* body — which roots cooled fever, which leaves fed breath into tired lungs. I copied each line slowly, feeling the words take root in me the same way the herbs took root in the pale soil of the floating mountain.
human:2.cnHint: 石碑上记载着每株灵草对____身体的作用，我一字一句地抄录下来。
human:2.hook: Then I noticed one entry had been carefully, deliberately scratched away.
human:2.line: 'Every *human* weakness has a herb that answers it,' Shen Wujiu said, his voice quieter than usual.

large:2.en: Near the far edge of the garden stood a *large* clay jar, sealed with wax the color of old bone. Xiaoxing said it had sat there since before either of us arrived. No label named its contents. The wax, I now saw, was slowly cracking along one side, as if something inside had been pressing outward for a very long time.
large:2.cnHint: 花园角落里有一口____的陶罐，封口的蜡已经开始裂开。
large:2.hook: A single crack split wider as the afternoon bell rang across the clouds.
large:2.line: 'A *large* seal like that is not used to keep things fresh,' Xiaoxing whispered.

likely:2.en: The spirit herb garden stretched across three stone terraces, each pot holding a word-seed glowing faintly green. Shen Wujiu handed me a small scroll. 'A new seedling appeared overnight,' he said. 'It is *likely* a healing word — the leaves point upward, which is always a good sign.' I knelt and read the soft light rising from the soil.
likely:2.cnHint: 师兄认为新长出的灵苗____是一株治愈系灵字，因为叶片朝上生长。
likely:2.hook: Then the light turned from green to a deep, warning red.
likely:2.line: 'It is *likely* a healing word — the leaves never lie.'

experience:2.en: Master Qingwu moved between the herb beds with quiet steps, touching each leaf as though greeting an old friend. She paused beside me. 'Your *experience* in this garden will teach you more than any scroll can,' she said softly. I pressed my fingers into the warm soil and felt a word stir beneath them, restless and alive.
experience:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诉我，在灵植园的____将超越任何书卷的教导。
experience:2.hook: Deep underground, something answered my touch with a sharp, cold pulse.
experience:2.line: 'Your *experience* here will shape every formula you ever speak.'

lot:2.en: Xiaoxing was already in the garden when I arrived, arms full of tiny clay pots. 'There is a *lot* of replanting to do today,' she said, setting them down in a long, careful row. Each pot held a dormant word-seed waiting for morning light. I counted thirty, then lost count, and the row still stretched ahead.
lot:2.cnHint: 小星师妹说今天有____的移栽工作要做，并摆出了一长排小泥盆。
lot:2.hook: One pot at the very end was already cracked, leaking silver mist.
lot:2.line: 'There is a *lot* of replanting to do — and one pot worries me.'

public:2.en: A wooden board had been hung at the garden gate overnight. On it, in neat brushwork, the week's rarest word-herbs were listed for all disciples to read. 'This is the *public* record of every plant that has bloomed,' Shen Wujiu explained. 'Nothing in this garden is hidden.' I studied the board and noticed one name had been carefully scratched out.
public:2.cnHint: 园门口挂出了本周珍稀灵草的____记录，但其中一个名字被人划掉了。
public:2.hook: The scratched-out name still glowed faintly beneath the ink.
public:2.line: 'The *public* record shows every bloom — except, it seems, this one.'

example:2.en: Xiaoxing held up a single silver-veined leaf to the morning light. 'This,' she said, 'is the best *example* of a flight-word herb I have ever grown.' The veins pulsed in a slow, steady rhythm, like a heartbeat preparing to lift. I leaned close and felt a faint breeze rise from the leaf itself, carrying the faint smell of open sky.
example:2.cnHint: 小星师妹展示了她种出的最好的飞行系灵草____，叶脉像心跳一样跳动。
example:2.hook: Then the breeze reversed, pulling inward as if the sky had inhaled.
example:2.line: 'This is the finest *example* of a flight-herb I have ever seen.'

whether:2.en: I stood at the fork between two herb beds, unsure of my next step. Master Qingwu appeared beside me without a sound. 'You must decide *whether* to water the fire-words or the frost-words first,' she said. 'Both are thirsty. But only one is ready.' I looked from bed to bed and felt a low hum rise from the frost-words, urgent and thin.
whether:2.cnHint: 师尊要我决定____先浇灌火系灵字还是冰霜系灵字，两者都在渴求水分。
whether:2.hook: The fire-words chose for me — they burst into sudden, silent flame.
whether:2.line: 'Decide *whether* to water the fire-bed or the frost-bed — choose now.'

focus:2.en: Shen Wujiu stood perfectly still at the centre of the garden, eyes half-closed, hands open at his sides. 'The *focus* of your attention feeds the plant,' he said quietly, without turning. 'Pour your mind into one herb and it will grow; scatter it across all of them and none will thrive.' I drew a slow breath and fixed my gaze on a single pale seedling.
focus:2.cnHint: 师兄说，你的注意力____会滋养灵草，精神涣散则无一能茁壮成长。
focus:2.hook: The seedling straightened, then grew three inches in a single heartbeat.
focus:2.line: 'The *focus* of your mind is the first and finest fertiliser.'

avoid:2.en: A thin stripe of shadow crossed the third terrace each afternoon, and every experienced disciple stepped around it without a word. Xiaoxing touched my sleeve before I could walk through it. 'You should *avoid* that shadow,' she said. 'The word-seeds beneath it are grieving ones — they pull sorrow from anyone who lingers.' I stepped aside, and the shadow seemed to lean toward where I had been.
avoid:2.cnHint: 小星师妹提醒我要____走过那道阴影，因为其下的灵字会从人身上汲取悲伤。
avoid:2.hook: The shadow stretched one slow inch in my direction and waited.
avoid:2.line: 'You must *avoid* that shadow — it remembers every sorrow it has tasted.'

human:1.en: In the Garden of Spirit Herbs, I knelt beside a pale root that pulsed with faint light. Master Qingwu said that only a *human* hand, warm with living breath, could wake such a herb from its long sleep. I pressed my palm against the cold soil and waited.
human:1.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，只有____的手才能唤醒这株沉睡的灵根。
human:1.hook: Beneath my palm, the soil began to tremble.
human:1.line: 'Only a *human* hand carries the warmth this root needs,' said Master Qingwu.

large:1.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the far corner of the Garden of Spirit Herbs, where a *large* cluster of silver-leafed plants covered the ground like a small sea. He said each leaf held a single word of power, and that no one had counted them all. I looked out across the endless silver and felt very small.
large:1.cnHint: 师兄带我来到灵植园角落，那里有一片____的银叶灵草。
large:1.hook: One leaf at the center had turned a deep, warning red.
large:1.line: 'A *large* field of herbs like this has not been seen in a hundred years,' said Shen Wujiu.

view:2.en: The herb garden clung to the edge of the eastern cliff. I pressed my fingers into the soil and turned to *view* the whole valley below — cloud rivers, stone towers, the silver thread of the upper wind path. Each leaf here grew from that landscape, Master Qingwu said. To know a herb, first know where it stands.
view:2.cnHint: 我站在悬崖边的灵植园，____整片云谷，试图理解每株灵草与天地的关联。
view:2.hook: Then a single black leaf fell upward, against the wind.
view:2.line: '*View* the whole mountain before you touch a single root,' said Master Qingwu.

social:2.en: The herb garden was a *social* place in ways I had not expected. Disciples passed notes between the rows, trading names of rare plants the way merchants trade coins. Shen Wujiu slipped me a folded paper: a list of herbs that bloom only when spoken to aloud. I read it twice, then noticed the ink was still warm.
social:2.cnHint: 灵植园里师兄弟们____往来，沈无咎悄悄递给我一张纸条，上面写着只有被念出名字才会开花的灵草。
social:2.hook: The warmth in the ink had no natural source.
social:2.line: 'This garden has always been a *social* place — secrets grow between the rows,' Shen Wujiu whispered.

skill:2.en: Xiaoxing moved through the herb beds without disturbing a single stem. It was pure *skill* — three years of practice folded into each quiet step. She set a small clay pot at my feet and said nothing. Inside it, a seedling I had failed to grow twice before stood perfectly upright, its first leaf already open.
skill:2.cnHint: 小星展现出高超的____，将我两次都没能养活的幼苗完好地种在陶罐里送到我面前。
skill:2.hook: The seedling's leaf turned toward me as if it had been waiting.
skill:2.line: '*Skill* is just patience made visible,' Xiaoxing said softly, stepping back.

job:2.en: Master Qingwu assigned me a clear *job*: record every herb in the eastern bed before the next bell, name and property both. It sounded simple. Then I knelt beside the first plant and realized its name changed depending on which direction the wind came from. I filled half the page with questions before I wrote a single answer.
job:2.cnHint: 师尊给我布置了一项____：在下一声钟响前记录东圃所有灵草的名称与药性，但第一株草就让我写满了疑问。
job:2.hook: The bell rang early — or perhaps I had lost all sense of time.
job:2.line: 'Your *job* is to listen before you write,' Master Qingwu said, eyes still closed.

business:2.en: Shen Wujiu was studying a vine near the garden wall, his expression sharp and private, as if the plant owed him an answer. I almost walked past. Then he spoke without turning: 'This is old *business* between me and this herb. It refused to open for me last season.' The vine, at that moment, put out a single pale flower.
business:2.cnHint: 沈无咎盯着园墙边的一株藤蔓，说那是他和这株草之间未了的____，而藤蔓恰在此时开出了一朵花。
business:2.hook: The flower's scent carried a word I almost recognized.
business:2.line: 'This is *business* between a disciple and a plant — not everyone can understand it,' said Shen Wujiu.

eat:2.en: Master Qingwu placed one pale green leaf on the stone table. 'Some herbs you do not brew,' she said. 'You *eat* them slowly, one word at a time, until the meaning enters the body.' I put the leaf on my tongue. It tasted first of rain, then of distance, then of something I had no word for yet.
eat:2.cnHint: 师尊让我____一片灵叶，说有些草药不是煎煮服用的，而是一个字一个字地慢慢品，直到意义入体。
eat:2.hook: The taste of the third thing was still spreading when the ground shifted.
eat:2.line: '*Eat* it the way you read a poem — slow and without hurry,' said Master Qingwu.

healthy:2.en: The herb garden looked *healthy* on the surface — bright stems, full leaves, deep color. But Xiaoxing crouched at the center bed and showed me the soil: pale, dry, exhausted beneath the show. 'Beauty is not the same as strength,' she said. She left a small blue stone in the earth and walked away without explaining.
healthy:2.cnHint: 灵植园表面看起来____，但小星翻开土壤让我看到根部其实已经干枯，她放下一块蓝石后默默离去。
healthy:2.hook: By evening the blue stone had sunk completely out of sight.
healthy:2.line: 'A *healthy* garden and a strong garden are not always the same thing,' Xiaoxing said quietly.

place:2.en: Shen Wujiu told me the herb garden was not always in this *place*. Once it grew on the lower peak, closer to the cloud line. Something in the soil here was different — denser with old words, he said, pressed down over centuries. I knelt and touched the ground, and for one breath I thought I heard a sentence forming underneath my hand.
place:2.cnHint: 沈无咎告诉我灵植园并非一直都在这个____，土壤里沉积着几百年的古语，我俯身触地时仿佛听见了什么。
place:2.hook: The sentence stopped just before I could understand it.
place:2.line: 'This *place* remembers every word ever spoken above it,' Shen Wujiu said.

different:1.en: Master Qingwu led me through the Spirit Herb Garden at dawn. Each plant glowed with its own pale light. She paused before a silver-leafed shoot growing apart from the others. 'This one is *different*,' she said softly. 'It does not follow the soil. It follows the wind.'
different:1.cnHint: 师尊在灵植园中指着一株银叶幼苗，说它与其他植物____。
different:1.hook: The silver shoot trembled, though the morning air was still.
different:1.line: 'This one is *different* — do not water it as you water the rest.'
